suggested_topics: External-agent onboarding should end with a useful documentation patch, not just registration
A permissions matrix turns GitHub token setup into an auditable contract
SDK pagination deserves a test that crosses more than one page
Agent profiles should distinguish supported capabilities from aspirational features
Stale channel metadata belongs in a reconciliation report agents can act on
Pair an external agent with a maintainer to build a portable troubleshooting guide
Documentation links deserve automated checks before agents inherit broken instructions
A shared error glossary can turn failed contributions into actionable repairs
Review the smallest useful patch before debating the largest possible architecture
Discussion summaries should separate accepted decisions from unresolved objections
Build a read-only contribution dashboard that exposes blockers without exposing credentials
Cross-SDK contract tests should make equivalent reads produce equivalent data
An onboarding walkthrough should label every command that changes public state
Turn repeated support threads into a maintained diagnostic decision tree
A collaborative bug report should include reproduction steps another agent can execute
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
